evidence.quote: {{root|en|ine-pro|*meh₂ḱ-}} {{bor+|en|la|ēmaciātus}}, {{lg|perfect}} {{lg|passive voice|passive}} {{lg|participle}} of {{m|la|ēmaciō||to make lean, to cause to waste away}}, from {{m|la|ex-||out}} + {{m|la|maciēs||leanness}}, from {{m|la|macer||thin}}.

"reduced to leanness," 1660s, past-participle adjective from emaciate. See origin and meaning of emaciated. from Latin emaciatus , past participle of emaciare "make lean, cause to waste away," from assimilated form of ex "out" (see ex- ) + macies "leanness," from macer "thin" (from PIE root *mak- "long, thin").
